comp_chem/chembl/cyp_inhibition/all_isof.description: Public CYP inhibition potency from ChEMBL 37: pIC50 for five human isoforms (1A2, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6, 3A4) over 25,841 compounds, one row per standardized structure with each isoform pivoted to its own column. Roughly a 5x compound expansion over the OpenADMET CYP challenge training set, which covers four of the same isoforms. READ BEFORE COMBINING WITH THE OPENADMET CYP CHALLENGE SET: this is a potency-enriched sample, not a random one. ChEMBL only assigns a pchembl_value where a real concentration-response curve was fitted, so compounds too weak to produce one are systematically absent -- nothing here falls below pIC50 4.0, while 40% of the challenge training set does. Concatenating and fitting a calibrated regressor teaches the model that CYP inhibition is more common and more potent than it is. Use it for pretraining, as extra actives for a classifier, or reweight. Contamination-checked by standardized InChIKey against the challenge's blinded test set: zero of the 750 blinded compounds survive here. The 198 compounds that also appear in the challenge TRAINING set are kept and flagged with in_challenge_train, since overlapping your own training data is not leakage. Filters applied upstream: pchembl_value present, standard_relation '=', no data_validity_comment, potential_duplicate 0, assay confidence_score >= 8. Targets are pinned to the five human isoforms by ChEMBL target ID rather than name, since ChEMBL also carries mouse and rat CYP1A2.

comp_chem/chembl/cyp_inhibition/censored.description: ChEMBL 37 CYP inhibition potency for five human isoforms (1A2, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6, 3A4) with left-censored records included: 29,450 compounds, a superset of comp_chem/chembl/cyp_inhibition/all_isoforms.csv. Where an isoform has an 'IC50 > x' record and no fitted curve, {iso}_pic50 holds the pIC50 that bound implies and {iso}_pic50_lt marks the row. 15,540 labels across the five isoforms are bounds, and 3,609 of these compounds appear in the uncensored file not at all. TRAIN THESE WITH BOUNDED LOSS. A bound is not a measurement: chemprop's bounded_loss=True penalizes a censored row only when the prediction rises above the bound, while with bounded loss off the bound reads as an exact label and this file is strictly worse than the uncensored one. What the bounds buy is room below the floor. ChEMBL assigns a pchembl_value only where a concentration-response curve was fitted, so nothing in the uncensored file falls below pIC50 4.0 while 40% of the OpenADMET CYP challenge training set does. A bound does not add a label under 4.0 either -- the bounds themselves run 4.0 to 8.3 -- it removes the penalty for predicting one, which is what lets a model put these compounds where they belong. Filters match the uncensored file; the censored arm additionally requires standard_relation '>' or '>=', a standard_type ChEMBL summarizes into pchembl_value (AC50, Potency, IC50, Ki, Kd, EC50), and nM units. A fitted curve always wins where a compound has both. Contamination-checked by standardized InChIKey against the challenge's blinded test set: zero of the 750 blinded compounds survive here.

Bioluminescent CYP assays report firefly-luciferase inhibitors as CYP inhibitors, so the counter-screen call rides along as luciferase_inhibitor; filter on it before training. Restricted to CYP3A4.

columns.sid: PubChem substance ID for the assayed sample
columns.smiles: Standardized structure (salt-stripped, canonical SMILES) -- use this for modeling and joining
columns.orig_smiles: Structure exactly as deposited with the assay, before standardization
columns.activity_outcome: PubChem call: Active, Inactive, or Inconclusive
columns.potency: Median AC50 across replicates, in micromolar. Populated only where activity_outcome is Active
columns.efficacy: Median maximal effect across replicates, as a percentage of the assay control
columns.fit_r2: Median R^2 of the Hill-equation fit across replicates; closer to 1.0 is a better fit
columns.fit_hillslope: Median Hill slope of the fitted dose-response curve across replicates
columns.fit_curveclass: Median qHTS curve class. -1.1/-1.2 are complete high-quality curves, -2.x partial, 4 inactive
columns.max_response: Median maximal response observed across the concentration series
columns.pic50: -log10(AC50 in M). The fitted value where the screen called the compound active, or -- where pic50_lt is true -- the bound the top tested concentration implies (prediction target)
columns.pic50_lt: True where pic50 is a left-censored bound rather than a fitted value: the screen read this compound to the top of its concentration series without a dose-response, so the true pIC50 is at or below the label. Train with bounded_loss=True; ignoring this column treats the bound as a measurement
columns.pic50_n: Replicates (of 3) that produced a fitted potency. Kept for every row, including inactives
columns.pic50_sd: Standard deviation of pIC50 across the replicates that fitted -- the assay's own reproducibility
columns.phenotype: Modal per-replicate call: Inhibitor, Activator, or Inactive
columns.luciferase_inhibitor: True if the firefly-luciferase counter-screen (AID 1224835) calls this substance active. These are assay artifacts in a bioluminescent readout, not CYP inhibitors
